full_judgment:
8. Mr. Abdur Razaque Khan, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellants, on reference to the judgment, submits that, the entire judgment is on surmises and conjecture and on reference to certain portion of the judgment, submits that, there is no materials in hand in arriving at such finding by the learned judge. Learned Advocate further submits that, defendants best case is that the suit land have been included in the census list but the defendant could not or did not prove when the suit land vested in the government. Learned Advocate further submit that, the case of the plaintiff is that the suit land was transferred in favour of the plaintiffs by original owner Pach Kori Das when he was in Bangladesh and this fact is supported by defendant Nos. 5 and 6 as they also purchased the suit land at the relevant time from Pachkori Das. and also by defendant No. 4, Narayangonj Pourashava, in his written statement supported the ease of the plaintiffs as such the impugned judgment as passed, was passed without considering these facts. Learned Advocate on reference to the written statement of the Government submits that, this written statement does not disclose anything excepting denial of the plaint case. It does not stated when the government included the suit property in the census list. Learned Advocate further submits that, the Government did not produce any evidence that the suit land was vested in the government as enemy property or as abandoned property. This learned Advocate further submits that plaintiff instituted the suit in 1993 and as per decision of the Appellate Division no property can be declared as enemy property or abandoned property after 1969. Learned Advocate in support of his submission relied on the decision of Government of Bangladesh vs Paresh Chandra Ghacami, 50 DLR (AD) 70, wherein it has been held that when the Government failed to prove the legal foundation for enlisting the suit property in the census report of the vested property and the plaintiffs led some evidence in support of their interest in the suit property the appellate Court decreed the suit on correct view of law. 

 9. The learned Advocate also relied on the case of Dayal Chandra Mondal vs Assistant Custodian of Vested and Non-Resident Properties (L & B) and Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue); Dhaka, 50 DLR 186 wherein it has been held that, claim by the Government or by the vested property authority that a certain property is a vested property by property is a vested property without the necessary factual basis and legal foundation has no validity in the eye of law. Laws relating to enemy properties now vested properties are fairly well-settled by now, properties which assumed enemy character and became enemy properties by operation of law during the relevant time viz from 6-9-65 to 16-2-69 when emergency was formally lifted, became vested properties and the Government may treat such properties as enemy or vested properties and take over possession thereof in accordance with law subject to the legitimate rights of co-owners, co-sharers and the bonafide transferees in lawful possession therein. But before a property is treated as vested property on the basis of a V.P. Case started long after the lifting of emergency on 16th February. 1969 a heavy duty is cast upon the authority concerned to satisfy itself that the recorded tenant migrated to India before 1965. 

 14. We also do not find such case, make out be the government in its written statement. Moreover, the decisions of the Appellate Division in the case of Arati Rani Paul vs Sudarshan Kumar Pal 56 DLR (AD) 73 and in the case of Luxmikanti Roy vs Upazila Nirbahi Officer, 46 DLR 136, Maram Mandal being dead his heirs Dayal Chandra Mandal vs. Assistant Custodian of Vested and Non-resident Property, 50 DLR 186, it has been held that since the law of enemy property itself died with the repeal of Ordinance 1 of 1969 on 23-3-1974 no further vested property case can be started thereafter on the basis of the law which is already dead.
